steps.say: A suspected testicular cancer is never biopsied through the scrotum. The testis is removed through a groin cut with the cord tied high at the internal ring. Cutting through scrotal skin seeds tumour into groin nodes and upstages the patient, so that route is forbidden.
steps.tx: **Radical inguinal orchiectomy** (groin removal of testis and cord) with high ligation of the spermatic cord at the **internal ring** (deep inguinal ring) is mandatory; **scrotal violation** (any scrotal skin breach) or trans-scrotal biopsy is strictly contraindicated. The cord is clamped high before the testis is handled, and histology is confirmed on the removed specimen, never on a scrotal sample.

vis.alt: Bisected orchiectomy specimen showing homogeneous fleshy seminoma.
vis.caption: Seminoma orchiectomy specimen; high inguinal removal precedes all therapy. Credit: Ed Uthman, MD.

steps.say: Blood markers stage the disease and track treatment. Alpha fetoprotein falls with a half life of five to seven days, beta HCG within twenty four to thirty six hours, and LDH reflects bulk. After removal the markers must fall on schedule, and a slow fall identifies residual disease.
steps.tx: Serum markers are **alpha-fetoprotein** (yolk sac marker, AFP), **beta-hCG** (choriocarcinoma marker, beta-human chorionic gonadotropin), and lactate dehydrogenase (bulk marker, LDH), each with its **half-life** (marker clearance time): AFP **5 to 7 days** (five to seven), beta-hCG **24 to 36 hours** (twenty four to thirty six). After orchiectomy markers must fall on schedule; slow clearance identifies residual disease and the nadir feeds prognostic grouping.

rows: Half-life 5 to 7 days, yolk sac elements
Post-treatment low point feeds prognostic grouping

steps.say: Alpha fetoprotein sets a hard diagnostic line. It never rises in pure seminoma or in pure choriocarcinoma. Any rise in a presumed seminoma forces treatment as a non seminomatous tumour, which needs different drugs and usually surgery.
steps.tx: AFP is never elevated in **pure seminoma** (uniform seminoma histology) or pure choriocarcinoma, so **AFP elevation** (raised alpha-fetoprotein) in a presumed seminoma mandates management as **NSGCT** (non-seminomatous germ cell tumour). The rule prevents under-treatment, since NSGCT needs different chemotherapy and usually post-chemotherapy surgery while pure seminoma follows its own pathway.

vis.alt: Diagram of testicular tumour pathology with seminoma cells and yolk sac elements.
vis.caption: Seminoma cells beside yolk sac elements; AFP rise identifies the non-seminoma component. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Spread follows the testicular vessels, not the scrotum. The right testis drains between the great vessels into interaortocaval nodes. The left testis drains beside the aorta near the left kidney. This highway explains why nodes behind the peritoneum are the first landing zone.
steps.tx: **Lymphatic drainage** (first landing-zone nodes) of the right testis runs to **interaortocaval nodes** (nodes between aorta and vena cava), while the left testis drains to **para-aortic nodes** (nodes beside the aorta) near the left renal hilum. This embryological highway makes retroperitoneal nodes the first landing zone, and explains why scrotal violation reroutes spread to the groin with such harm.

rows: Para-aortic nodes near left renal hilum
Drainage follows testicular vessels, not scrotum
Reroutes spread to groin nodes, upstages patient

steps.say: Node surgery must protect ejaculation. The template removes landing zone nodes while sparing the sympathetic fibres around the first to third lumbar levels. These fibres drive forward ejaculation through the vas and bladder neck, so most patients keep fertility potential after nerve sparing surgery.
steps.tx: **Nerve-sparing RPLND** (sympathetic-preserving node dissection) preserves postganglionic sympathetic fibers of the **hypogastric plexus** (autonomic network) at **L1 to L3** (first to third lumbar levels) to maintain **antegrade ejaculation** (forward ejaculation through vas and bladder neck). The template clears landing-zone nodes while these microscopic fibers stay intact, so most patients retain fertility potential.

rows: Postganglionic sympathetic fibres of hypogastric plexus
L1 to L3 around aorta and cava
Clears landing-zone nodes, spares microscopic fibres

steps.say: Leftover masses after chemotherapy are removed in non seminoma. A residual lump over one centimetre with normal markers needs complete surgical removal, because teratoma or live cancer hides inside most of them. This operation is harder than primary surgery, and complete removal decides cure.
steps.tx: Post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal **residual mass** (leftover lump after drugs) in NSGCT over **1 cm** (one centimetre) with normalized markers mandates complete excision by **post-chemotherapy RPLND** (redo node dissection), because **teratoma** (mature chemo-resistant tissue) or viable cancer hides inside most of them. The operation is harder than primary surgery, and completeness of resection decides cure.

rows: Teratoma or viable cancer in most cases

steps.say: Seminoma leftovers behave differently. Lumps under three centimetres after chemotherapy are watched, since scar tissue is the rule. Larger lumps need a PET scan at least six to eight weeks after drugs to test for live tumour before any surgery is considered.
steps.tx: **Post-chemo seminoma** (seminoma after chemotherapy) residual masses **under 3 cm** (three centimetres) are managed with surveillance, since fibrosis is the rule. Lesions reaching **3 cm** need **FDG PET-CT** (metabolic imaging) no earlier than **6 to 8 weeks** (six to eight) after chemotherapy to check for live tumour before surgery is considered, since removing dead fibrosis benefits nobody.

rows: FDG PET-CT at 6 to 8 weeks post-chemotherapy
Test metabolic activity before any surgery
Helps nobody, avoid without PET guidance

steps.say: Prognosis is grouped, not guessed. The IGCCCG system sorts widespread germ cell tumours into good, intermediate, and poor groups using the primary site, spread beyond the lungs, and the marker low point. The group predicts cure rates and sets how intense the chemotherapy must be.
steps.tx: The **IGCCCG criteria** (International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group model) sort metastatic germ cell tumours into good, intermediate, and poor **prognostic groups** (predicted-outcome groups) by primary site, non-pulmonary visceral metastases, and marker nadir. The group predicts cure rates and selects chemotherapy intensity, from lighter regimens in good-risk disease to full-dose therapy and trials in poor-risk patients.

rows: Good, intermediate, or poor; sets drug intensity
